control_architecture: early task-decomposition; tactile feedback for object manipulation
creator: Waseda University, Kato Laboratory
disclosure_citation: Kato, Ichiro et al. 'Information-Power Machine with Senses and Limbs (WABOT-1).' Proceedings of First CISM-IFToMM Symposium on Theory and Practice of Robots and Manipulators, 1973.
notes: The Waseda lineage is the deep root of academic humanoid robotics. WABOT-2 (1984) added musical performance capability. || v0.2 migration: Foundational academic prior art. The 1973 CISM-IFToMM paper discloses essentially every major humanoid subsystem at concept level.
prior_art_notes: First full-scale humanoid in academic record. Anticipates virtually every subsystem of modern humanoids at concept level: bipedal locomotion, bimanual manipulation, multimodal sensing, natural language interface. Specific implementations are crude by modern standards but the architectural decomposition is foundational.
sensing: artificial vision, tactile sensors, artificial ears for command recognition
sources: Kato, I. et al. 1973 CISM-IFToMM Symposium proceedings.
Waseda University Humanoid Robotics Institute archives.

control_architecture: Simplex: high-assurance simple controller with verified safety envelope, alongside complex high-performance controller, with a decision module that switches to the simple controller when complex controller violates envelope
creator: Lui Sha, Carnegie Mellon University
disclosure_citation: Sha, Lui. 'Dependable system upgrade.' Proceedings 19th IEEE Real-Time Systems Symposium, 1998. Earlier conceptual work circa 1995.
ip_citations: academic publication; concept widely adopted without IP enforcement
notable_capabilities: formal safety guarantees in presence of complex/unverified control
backbone of much modern safety-critical control
notes: Simplex is among the most-cited safety architecture concepts in real-time and cyber-physical systems literature.
prior_art_notes: Foundational prior art for safety supervisor architectures in robotics and physical AI. Any 'safety supervisor' or 'safety envelope' or 'fallback controller' patent claim post-1995 must contend with Sha's Simplex work as anticipating prior art. Directly relevant to MathGround's Simplex supervisor architecture.
sources: Sha, L. 'Using Simplicity to Control Complexity.' IEEE Software 18(4), 2001.
Crenshaw, T.L. et al. 'The Simplex reference model: limiting fault-propagation due to unreliable components in cyber-physical system architectures.' RTSS 2007.

creator: AIST (National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology), Kawada Industries
disclosure_citation: Kaneko, K. et al. 'Design of prototype humanoid robotics platform for HRP.' IROS 2002.
ip_citations: AIST academic publications; OpenHRP simulation framework released openly
notes: The HRP series is one of the longest-running humanoid programs and produced significant open-source simulation infrastructure. || v0.2 migration: Kanehiro et al. IJRR 2004 OpenHRP paper is the foundational open-architecture humanoid simulation prior art. AIST published extensively, making this entry well-documented.
prior_art_notes: OpenHRP is itself foundational prior art for open robotics simulation frameworks. HRP-2 was among the first humanoids to publicly demonstrate falling-and-recovering behaviors.
sources: Kanehiro, F. et al. 'OpenHRP: Open Architecture Humanoid Robotics Platform.' IJRR 23(2), 2004.

control_architecture: ZMP balancing; later versions added DRC-specific manipulation behaviors
creator: KAIST, Hubo Lab (Jun-Ho Oh)
disclosure_citation: Park, Ill-Woo et al. 'Mechanical Design of Humanoid Robot Platform KHR-3 (HUBO).' IEEE-RAS Humanoids 2005.
ip_citations: KAIST academic program; design papers published openly
notes: The Korean academic humanoid program is among the deepest in the world; HUBO lineage has multiple commercial spinouts. || v0.2 migration: DRC-Hubo's bipedal/wheeled transformation is among the few clear disclosures of mode-switching humanoid locomotion.
prior_art_notes: DRC-Hubo's 2015 win demonstrated transformer-style transitioning between bipedal and wheeled-knee modes for navigating both stairs and flat ground. Anticipates: hybrid locomotion modes in humanoids.
sources: Park, I.-W. et al. IEEE-RAS Humanoids 2005.

control_architecture: Computes backward-reachable sets representing states from which a safety-violating state can be forced by adversary inputs; produces verified safe controllers
creator: Ian Mitchell, Alexandre Bayen, Claire Tomlin (UC Berkeley/Stanford)
disclosure_citation: Mitchell, I.M., Bayen, A.M., Tomlin, C.J. 'A time-dependent Hamilton-Jacobi formulation of reachable sets for continuous dynamic games.' IEEE TAC 50(7), 2005.
notable_capabilities: formally verified safety in continuous nonlinear systems
notes: Tomlin's group at UCB has been the most prolific source of HJ reachability applications.
prior_art_notes: Foundational prior art for formally-verified safe control. Any patent claiming 'verified safety envelopes' or 'formal safety guarantees' for autonomous systems must contend with HJ reachability work.
sources: Mitchell, I.M. et al. IEEE TAC 50(7), 2005.
Bansal, S. et al. 'Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability: A Brief Overview and Recent Advances.' CDC 2017.

control_architecture: Defines speed and separation monitoring, power and force limiting, hand guiding, safety-rated monitored stop
creator: ISO TC 299 (Robotics) working group
disclosure_citation: ISO 10218-1:2006 'Robots and robotic devices — Safety requirements for industrial robots — Part 1: Robots.' International Organization for Standardization.
notable_capabilities: industry-standard safety modes for collaborative robots
categorical safety requirements for power-and-force-limited operation
notes: Including standards documents in the corpus is a deliberate choice: they are publicly disclosed, dated, and constitute defensive prior art for claims in their domain.
prior_art_notes: ISO 10218 (and the related ISO/TS 15066 for collaborative operation) constitute foundational prior art for collaborative robot safety claims. Any patent claim around 'safety-rated monitored stop,' 'speed and separation monitoring,' or 'power and force limiting' in collaborative robotics is anticipated by these standards.

creator: Waseda University, Takanishi Laboratory
disclosure_citation: Ogura, Y. et al. 'Development of a New Humanoid Robot WABIAN-2.' ICRA 2006.
notable_capabilities: designed as a human walking research platform
notes: Continues the Waseda lineage from WABOT-1. WABIAN-2R is a refined variant.
prior_art_notes: WABIAN-2's stretched-knee gait disclosure is significant prior art for any humanoid walking control claim aiming at more human-like locomotion (less crouched, more upright knees during stance). Distinct from ASIMO's bent-knee paradigm. The Takanishi laboratory's continued publication makes this a well-anchored academic disclosure.

control_architecture: Lyapunov-like functions that certify forward invariance of a safe set under a control law; can be composed with QP-based controllers for online safety filtering
creator: Peter Wieland and Frank Allgöwer (early formalization); Aaron Ames and others (modern formalization)
disclosure_citation: Wieland, P. and Allgöwer, F. 'Constructive safety using control barrier functions.' IFAC Proceedings Volumes 40(12), 2007.
notable_capabilities: composable with arbitrary nominal controllers via QP
applied across robotics, vehicles, multi-agent systems
notes: The Ames 2017 paper is the most-cited modern reference; the Wieland 2007 paper is the deeper prior art origin.
prior_art_notes: CBFs are the dominant modern formalism for online safety filtering in robotics. Substantial prior art for any patent claiming online safety filtering, safety-aware QP control, or formally-bounded safe ML execution. Particularly relevant to MathGround's Universal Fuzz Law work as the formal foundation for safety envelopes.
sources: Wieland, P. and Allgöwer, F. IFAC 2007.
Ames, A.D. et al. 'Control Barrier Function Based Quadratic Programs for Safety Critical Systems.' IEEE TAC 62(8), 2017.
Ames, A.D. et al. 'Control Barrier Functions: Theory and Applications.' ECC 2019.

control_architecture: YARP middleware; behavior-based and learning approaches
creator: Italian Institute of Technology (IIT) and the RobotCub Consortium
disclosure_citation: Metta, G. et al. 'The iCub humanoid robot: an open platform for research in embodied cognition.' PerMIS 2008.

ip_citations: GPL/LGPL software; CAD released under open license; iCub.org repository

The tendon-driven 9-DoF hand is similarly foundational.
prior_art_notes: Among the earliest fully open-source humanoid platforms with hardware design released. Anticipates: tendon-driven anthropomorphic hands, full-body artificial skin, open robotics middleware.
sensing: stereo cameras, microphones, force-torque, full-body tactile skin

actuator_details: Harmonic-drive electric servos with dust/water resistance
creator: AIST and Kawada Industries
disclosure_citation: Kaneko, K. et al. 'Humanoid Robot HRP-3.' IROS 2008.
prior_art_notes: HRP-3's environmental sealing disclosures anticipate subsequent IP-rated humanoid claims. The HRP series is a deep commons asset because of consistent open academic disclosure across generations.

actuator_details: Cable-driven actuators; intrinsically safe by design
creator: Willow Garage / Stanford (Ken Salisbury group)
disclosure_citation: Wyrobek, K.A. et al. 'Towards a Personal Robotics Development Platform: Rationale and Design of an Intrinsically Safe Personal Robot.' ICRA 2008.
ip_citations: academic publication; Willow Garage open release tradition
notes: Predates PR2 and established the safety-conscious design philosophy.
prior_art_notes: PR1 is significant prior art for safety-by-design humanoid robotics. Cable-driven intrinsically-safe architecture anticipates several modern compliant-actuator humanoid claims.

control_architecture: Runtime monitor that switches between primary and verified backup controller based on safety constraint satisfaction
creator: Air Force Research Laboratory and DARPA program
disclosure_citation: Schierman, J.D. et al. 'Runtime Assurance Framework Development for Highly Adaptive Flight Control Systems.' Air Force Research Laboratory, 2015. Earlier DARPA AACUS work circa 2010.
ip_citations: AFRL technical reports; DARPA-funded; broadly published
notable_capabilities: enables fielding of unverified ML-based controllers in safety-critical aviation
notes: AFRL RTA work is widely cited but underappreciated outside aerospace. Worth surfacing in robotics-domain prior art arguments.
prior_art_notes: Direct descendant of Simplex; the 'unverified neural net plus verified safety controller' pattern. Anticipates modern ML-safety supervisor patents in autonomous vehicles, drones, and robotics. Directly applicable as prior art to safety claims in physical AI products.

creator: AIST and Kawada Industries
disclosure_citation: Kaneko, K. et al. 'Humanoid Robot HRP-4: Humanoid Robotics Platform with Lightweight and Slim Body.' IROS 2010.
notes: HRP-4C (separate variant, focused on female-form humanoid for entertainment) is a related but distinct entry not included here.
prior_art_notes: HRP-4 lightweight design anticipates subsequent slim-form humanoid claims. The 2010 IROS paper provides full mechanical specifications openly.

actuator_details: Tendon-driven hands with extraordinarily high finger DoF; series-elastic in some joints
creator: NASA Johnson Space Center, in partnership with General Motors
disclosure_citation: Diftler, M.A. et al. 'Robonaut 2 — The First Humanoid Robot in Space.' ICRA 2011.
end_effector: five-fingered tendon-driven hands, 12 DoF per hand
ip_citations: NASA-GM joint patents; many subsequently licensed broadly
notes: R2 was retired from ISS in 2018; design legacy continues through Valkyrie and through GM industrial humanoid work.
prior_art_notes: Robonaut 2's hand design, with 12 DoF per hand and tendon routing through the forearm, is foundational prior art for high-DoF tendon-driven humanoid hands. The NASA-GM patent portfolio has been extensively cited.
sources: Bridgwater, L.B. et al. 'The Robonaut 2 Hand — Designed To Do Work With Tools.' ICRA 2012.

actuator_details: Series-elastic actuators throughout; rotary and linear
creator: NASA Johnson Space Center, in collaboration with University of Texas at Austin and others
disclosure_citation: NASA Johnson Space Center, DARPA Robotics Challenge entry, 2013.
notes: Among the most thoroughly published private-but-open humanoid platforms.
prior_art_notes: NASA Valkyrie's series-elastic actuator implementations and the IHMC-derived whole-body control work are foundational prior art. The robot was distributed to multiple universities and produced extensive open publications.
sources: Radford, N. et al. 'Valkyrie: NASA's First Bipedal Humanoid Robot.' Journal of Field Robotics 32(3), 2015.

actuator_details: Series-elastic actuators with fiberglass leaf-spring legs implementing the spring-loaded inverted pendulum (SLIP) model
creator: Oregon State University, Dynamic Robotics Laboratory (Jonathan Hurst)
disclosure_citation: Hubicki, C. et al. 'ATRIAS: Design and validation of a tether-free 3D-capable spring-mass bipedal robot.' International Journal of Robotics Research 35(12), 2016.
ip_citations: academic publication; OSU patents licensed widely
notable_capabilities: first machine to walk in 3D space using passive-dynamics-inspired control
demonstrated robust unscripted human-like walking gaits
notes: Direct ancestor of Cassie which became the basis for Agility Robotics' Digit. The Hurst-lab academic chain is among the most-cited in modern bipedal robotics.
prior_art_notes: ATRIAS is foundational prior art for spring-mass bipedal locomotion. The SLIP-based reduced-order control approach has become a dominant paradigm in dynamic bipedal walking, anticipating many subsequent commercial control claims.
sources: Hurst, J. et al. various IROS and ICRA publications, 2012-2015.

actuator_details: First-generation high-torque electric actuators with custom motor design
creator: MIT Biomimetic Robotics Lab (Sangbae Kim)
disclosure_citation: Seok, S. et al. 'Design principles for energy-efficient legged locomotion and implementation on the MIT Cheetah robot.' IEEE/ASME Transactions on Mechatronics 20(3), 2015. Earlier ICRA 2013 disclosure.
notes: Sometimes referred to as 'Cheetah 1'; the lab numbering is informal. Direct ancestor of all subsequent MIT Cheetah-family designs.
prior_art_notes: First-generation MIT Cheetah established the design principles for high-torque electric quadrupeds. Seok 2015 T-Mech paper provides foundational design-principles disclosure that anticipates many subsequent legged-robot actuation claims.
sources: Seok, S. et al. IEEE/ASME T-Mech 20(3), 2015.

creator: MIT Biomimetic Robotics Lab (Sangbae Kim)
disclosure_citation: Park, H.-W. et al. 'High-speed bounding with the MIT Cheetah 2: Control design and experiments.' International Journal of Robotics Research 36(2), 2017. Earlier ICRA disclosure 2014.
ip_citations: MIT academic publications; Wensing 2017 T-RO paper on actuator design
notes: Original MIT Cheetah (1) was hydraulic; Cheetah 2 transitioned to electric QDD which became the architectural standard.
prior_art_notes: MIT Cheetah 2 establishes the QDD actuator topology in a working high-speed legged robot. The Wensing 2017 T-RO paper 'Proprioceptive actuator design in the MIT Cheetah' is the foundational actuator design disclosure.
sources: Wensing, P.M. et al. 'Proprioceptive actuator design in the MIT Cheetah.' IEEE T-RO 33(3), 2017.

creator: Oregon State University, Dynamic Robotics Laboratory (Jonathan Hurst)
disclosure_citation: Agility Robotics / Oregon State University Cassie release, 2017.
notable_capabilities: Guinness record for fastest 100m by bipedal robot

prior_art_notes: Cassie and the broader Hurst lab work on reduced-order locomotion models is significant prior art for bipedal control claims industry-wide.

control_architecture: Synthesized reactive shield monitors RL agent actions and overrides any action that could violate temporal-logic safety specification
creator: Mohammed Alshiekh, Roderick Bloem, Rüdiger Ehlers, Bettina Könighofer, Scott Niekum, Ufuk Topcu
disclosure_citation: Alshiekh, M. et al. 'Safe Reinforcement Learning via Shielding.' AAAI 2018.
notable_capabilities: formal safety guarantees during RL training and deployment
temporal logic specification of safety properties
notes: Particularly relevant to physical AI deployment patents where ML-based control is wrapped in formal safety mechanisms.
prior_art_notes: Major prior art for any patent on RL safety filtering, shielded ML, or temporal-logic-bounded RL. Combined with Simplex and CBF prior art, makes much of the 'safe ML' patent space difficult to defend.
sources: Subsequent work by Könighofer, Bloem, others.

creator: MIT Biomimetic Robotics Lab (Sangbae Kim)
disclosure_citation: Bledt, G. et al. 'MIT Cheetah 3: Design and Control of a Robust, Dynamic Quadruped Robot.' IROS 2018.
notes: Cheetah 3 was directly downscaled into the Mini Cheetah platform.
prior_art_notes: Cheetah 3 establishes blind robust legged locomotion using only proprioceptive sensing — a significant prior art point against later vision-dependent legged-robot claims.

actuator_details: High-power harmonic-drive servos with wide range of motion
creator: AIST and Kawada Industries
disclosure_citation: Kaneko, K. et al. 'Humanoid Robot HRP-5P: An Electrically Actuated Humanoid Robot With High-Power and Wide-Range Joints.' IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters 4(2), 2019.
notes: Continues the HRP series' uninterrupted open-academic disclosure tradition.
prior_art_notes: HRP-5P's construction-task demonstrations and high-power actuator disclosures are among the most thoroughly published examples of humanoid construction work. Anticipates many subsequent industrial humanoid claims.
sources: Kaneko, K. et al. IEEE RA-L 4(2), 2019.

creator: MIT Biomimetic Robotics Lab (Sangbae Kim)
disclosure_citation: Katz, B. et al. 'Mini Cheetah: A Platform for Pushing the Limits of Dynamic Quadruped Control.' ICRA 2019.
ip_citations: academic publication; QDD design widely replicated
notes: Wensing 2017 is the deeper actuator paper; Katz 2019 is the integrated platform paper. || v0.2 migration: Wensing et al. T-RO 2017 'Proprioceptive actuator design in the MIT Cheetah' is the deep actuator prior art; Katz et al. ICRA 2019 is the integrated platform prior art. Together they anticipate the QDD topology now widely deployed.

sources: Wensing, P. et al. 'Proprioceptive actuator design in the MIT Cheetah.' IEEE T-RO 2017.

actuator_details: Series-elastic actuators in legs; direct-drive wheels

control_architecture: VLA model leveraging vision-language pretraining for manipulation

control_architecture: cross-embodiment learning from heterogeneous robot data
creator: 34-lab international collaboration coordinated by Google DeepMind
disclosure_citation: Open X-Embodiment Collaboration. 'Open X-Embodiment: Robotic Learning Datasets and RT-X Models.' arXiv 2310.08864, October 2023.

creator: UC Berkeley, Hybrid Robotics Lab
disclosure_citation: Liao, Q. et al. 'Berkeley Humanoid: A Research Platform for Learning-based Control.' arXiv 2024.
